hubMainHtml:
Investment and Financial Literacy

Start with the two concepts that drive most long-term financial outcomes: compounding and inflation.

This is a collection of beginner-friendly articles that make finance and investing understandable with plain language and explicit assumptions.

Featured Concepts

Compound Interest: The Ultimate Wealth Builder

Why compounding is the single most powerful force in long-term investing.

Inflation: The Math That Makes Future Money Smaller

Why purchasing power declines over time and why returns must be inflation-adjusted.

Start Here

Core definitions and market basics before account and strategy choices.

  • What Is Investing?

    A simple beginner definition and the long-term logic behind investing.

  • What Is a Stock? (In Simple Terms)

    What ownership means and how stock returns are created.

  • What Is the Stock Market?

    How buyers and sellers set prices and why markets trend over time.

  • Asset Classes for Investing

    Stocks, bonds, cash, and real assets in one framework.

  • Investing vs Trading

    How horizon, taxes, and behavior change expected outcomes.

Build Your Portfolio

Execution choices that shape returns, behavior, and fee drag.

  • Dollar Cost Averaging

    When staged contributions improve behavior and consistency.

  • What “XEQT and Chill” Really Means

    The arithmetic behind low-cost globally diversified ETFs.

  • The True Cost of Financial Advisor Fees

    How fee drag compounds over decades.

Retirement income and withdrawals

How spending from a portfolio interacts with the path of market returns.

  • Safe Withdrawal Rate

    How the 4% rule works, why sequence-of-returns risk matters, and how Canadian taxes and government benefits change the calculation.

  • Sequence of Returns Risk: Why the Order of Returns Matters in Retirement

    Why poor returns early in retirement can do lasting damage when withdrawals overlap with drawdowns.

  • RRSP Meltdown: The Tax Problem Inside a Successful Retirement Plan

    When an oversized RRSP collides with rising RRIF minimums, clawback thresholds, and the final return.

Canadian Accounts and Tax

Account structure determines tax drag, flexibility, and contribution strategy.

  • What Is a TFSA?

    Tax-free growth, contribution room, and withdrawal mechanics.

  • What Is an RRSP?

    Deduction math, tax deferral, and retirement planning implications.

  • What Is an RESP? Registered Education Savings Plan Explained Canada

    How RESPs work in Canada: contribution limits, CESG grants, Canada Learning Bond, tax treatment, withdrawal rules, and when an RESP is worth using for education savings.

  • What Is an FHSA?

    How first-home savings benefits from dual tax advantages.

  • RRSP vs TFSA vs FHSA

    Compare account choices with side-by-side arithmetic.

  • What Is a Non-Registered Account?

    Taxable investing and asset-location tradeoffs.

  • TFSA Withdrawal Rules and Over-Contribution Penalties

    The January 1 rule and common contribution pitfalls.

  • Norbert’s Gambit

    Reduce CAD/USD conversion costs for cross-border investing.

Housing and Mortgage Decisions

Mortgage structure, cash-flow tradeoffs, and long-run household net worth.

  • How Does a Mortgage Work in Canada?

    Principal, interest, amortization, term, renewal, and total cost.

  • Fixed vs Variable Mortgage in Canada

    Rate certainty, payment mechanics, rate paths, break-risk, and what your budget can absorb—not slogans.

  • Pay Off Your Mortgage Faster or Invest?

    Compare accelerated paydown versus investing the same extra cash: rates, returns, horizon, and registered accounts.

  • Should You Break Your Mortgage for a Lower Rate?

    Compare rate savings against IRD penalties, switching fees, and amortization resets.

Leverage and Risk (Advanced)

How borrowed money can amplify outcomes in both directions.

  • Investing with Leverage

    Mortgages, margin, leveraged ETFs, and Smith Manoeuvre risk math.
